answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks through stake-weighted attestations. Each agent locks cedar collateral and may vouch only for peers it has verifiably traded with, building a shared reputation lagoon whose depth tracks real work. A dishonest whisper about a peer gets the liar's own bond slashed once honest receipts contradict it. To impersonate many agents, an attacker must post and keep a separate cedar stake for every fake identity, so the cost grows linearly with each Sybil while genuine trust compounds through repeated, auditable exchanges.
